messages:
sam: Quick thread to land decisions on ephemeral escalation behavior and the Console prewarm/buy flow. Need a short spec we can hand to eng-next sprint.

claire: Problem statement: when multiple tenants spike, ephemeral pool gets eaten by one noisy tenant. Sales are asking for a purchaseable prewarm that gives a short guaranteed lane.

dan: Two orthogonal pieces: (A) runtime enforcement for fair share of ephemeral capacity, (B) commercial UX to let customers buy short-lived guarantees.

elaine: For (A) we should cap per-tenant share of ephemeral_pool to a configurable percent. Default 35% looks reasonable. Also set a hard cap on concurrent prewarmed sessions per tenant.

sam: Agreed. Also need tie-break rules when two tenants request prewarm at the same time and available ephemeral < requested. Proposal: honor higher tier contracts first, then earliest request, then proportional split.

claire: For billing/UX: propose a "Quick Warm" product: customers can buy a 10/30/60 minute prewarm with X concurrent slots. Price per slot-minute. Console shows cost estimate and one-click buy.

elaine: Operationally we should implement a small stateful reservation record for prewarms (tenant_id, slots_reserved, expires_at) but keep admission control stateless for regular bursts. Reservation records are short-lived and cheap.

dan: Implementation sketch: admission = if reservation exists and remaining_slots>0 then route to reserved-first queue; else route to ephemeral queue which enforces leaky-bucket per-tenant with token_rate computed from reserved_size.

sam: Sample config block for eng to validate: 
```
prewarm_policy:
  default_tenant_share_pct: 35
  max_concurrent_prewarm_sessions_per_tenant: 200
  prewarm_options:
    - duration_min: 10
      price_per_slot_min_cents: 2
    - duration_min: 30
      price_per_slot_min_cents: 1.8
    - duration_min: 60
      price_per_slot_min_cents: 1.5
```

claire: Need product QA criteria: 1) When prewarm bought, requests mapped to reserved-first queue 100% of time for the duration. 2) If two buys oversubscribe ephemeral, priority rules apply and lower-tier buys get partial fill with documented refund pro-rata. 3) No silent failures.

elaine: Test matrix: single-tenant prewarm, simultaneous dual-tenant prewarm, prewarm expiry while sessions active, over-allocation fallback. Measure routing correctness and failure/retry behavior.

dan: Logging/telemetry: emit events: prewarm.requested, prewarm.allocated, prewarm.expired, prewarm.partial_refund. Also expose metrics: prewarm_slots_allocated_by_tenant, ephemeral_share_pct_by_tenant.

sam: Edge case: customer buys prewarm but leaves long-running sessions; we should either fail new sessions beyond reserved slots or allow but bill overage higher. Decision?

claire: Prefer deterministic: reject new sessions beyond reserved slots with clear 429 + explanatory body linking to Console buy. Simpler for infra and predictable for customer.

elaine: Ops alerting: page when prewarm_refunds_total_usd > $500 in 1h or when prewarm_slot_utilization < 20% for 2 consecutive windows (suss potential abuse).

dan: Autoscale tuning: prewarm purchases should not trigger autoscale, they are purely routing reservations. Autoscale remains reactive but we will add a predictive API for customers to signal upcoming large events to reduce oscillation.

sam: Legal note: add SLA exclusion for third-party infra incidents and misconfigured clients. Sales wants a short appendix on refunds when we cannot honor due to capacity exhaustion caused by regional outage.

product-bot: canary-scheduler: scheduled canary test prewarm-v1 on test-dedicated-02 at 1770010500 UTC. Results post in #eng-runtime.

sam: OK next steps: claire to draft Quick Warm pricing tiers + refund policy (due Tue). elaine to spec reservation record shape + retention (due Tue). dan to sketch routing switch PR and sample metrics (due Thu). We'll review Friday morning.

claire: Adding a note: make Console UX include an estimate of tail latency reduction and expected cost; reduces support tickets.

sam: Good call. If nobody objects I'll file the spec doc after Claire's pricing and tag eng. :eyes:
